full_judgment:
Mr. Mainur Reza Chowdhury, J. : The leave petitioner and three others were facing trial before the Upazila (now Thana) Magistrate, Kalihati under Section 467/34 of the Penal Code on the basis of a written complaint filed by one Md. Moyezuddin. The allegation was that the accused petitioner and the other accused persons created a forged deed of sale on 13.2.1969 by using the name of Ayezuddin and his two brothers by false personation and there-after submitted the certified copy of the said deed before the Kalihati Upazila Revenue Officer for mutation of their names. The accused persons taking advantage of the fact that sub-registry office Bhuapur was destroyed by fire, created a kabala in respect of the land which the complainant was possessing. The trial court after considering the evidence on record found in the disputed deed that the land covered by the deed was described as land being in the district of Tangail, although on the date of registration of the deed that is on 13.2.1969, there was no existence of the district Tangail. The trial court therefore found the deed to have been forged and convicted the petitioners under Section 467 of the Penal Code and sentenced each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years and to pay fine of Tk. 1000/- in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three months. The petitioner then preferred an appeal being Criminal Appeal No. 91 of 1991 before the Second Additional Sessions Judge, Tangail in Criminal Appeal No. 91 of 1991 who confirmed the conviction and sentence passed by the trial court i.e. Additional District Magistrate, Tangail in C.R. Case No. 64(1)86. Against this judgment of affirmance the petitioner filed criminal revisional application before the High Court Division being Criminal Revision No. 1756 of 1993. The High Court Division was satisfied that on the date of registration of the deed on 13.2.69 at Bhuapur Sub-Registry office there was no existence of Tangail district and that during the relevant period Bhuapur Sub-Registry office was destroyed by fire. The High Court Division found that entire file of the mutation case was called for by the trial court and the same was in the record of the lower court. 

 2. It was also found that the application for mutation case was filed by Petitioner No. 2 which signature is same as that appearing in the vokalatnama. So, there was no doubt that the application form for mutation was filed by the petitioners and the certified copy of the deed was also filed with the application for mutation, although there was no evidence that the accused persons had created the deed by way of forgery. But there was evidence that they had filed a forged certified copy of a non-existent deed and as such their conviction was found to be legal and proper. The High Court Division did not accept the law point raised by the learned Counsel for the petitioner that the deed was submitted before a revenue court, and as no complaint was filed by the revenue court the case was barred under provisions of Section 195(I)(c) of Cr.P.C. Although it was true that the deed was filed for the purpose of mutation it would not be barred under the above provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure because the Upazila Revenue Officer did not per-form the function of revenue court when dealing with a mutation case. The High Court Division therefore discharged the rule upholding their conviction under Section 467 of the Code of Criminal Procedure but reduced the sentence of the petitioners to two years simple imprisonment instead of three years and liable to pay fine imposed by the trial court and confirmed by the lower appellate court. 

 3. The High Court Division rightly held that Section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure was not applicable in the present case as the upazila revenue officer did not perform the function of a revenue court when dealing with a mutation case. The High Court Division also rightly agreed with the findings of courts below that the petitioner had filed a certified copy of a forged deed before the upazila revenue officer for the purpose of mutation.
